title: FP8/INT8 Kernel Benchmarking Sprint — Charter
author: Talia Benson
body:
## Summary
This sprint quantifies and improves Redwood’s quantization-friendly execution paths (FP8 and INT8) in the serving runtime. The focus is on kernel behavior and scheduler interactions under realistic hosted traffic shapes, producing defensible results and shipping a small set of high-confidence improvements behind safe rollout controls.

We will measure both kernel-level performance (microbenchmarks) and end-to-end serving metrics (TTFT/TPOT/throughput) across top hosted models and primary GPU SKUs. The sprint concludes with a written report, repeatable methodology, and perf-canary gating.

---

## Objectives
1) Produce a defensible benchmark report for FP8 and INT8 across Redwood’s top hosted models and primary GPU SKUs.
2) Identify and land a small set of high-confidence kernel/scheduler changes (or default configuration changes) that improve cost-per-token and p95 latency without regressing correctness/quality.
3) Establish repeatable benchmarking methodology and automation: pinned environments, standardized workloads, regression thresholds, and dashboards.

---

## Why now
Quantized inference paths are becoming default for cost-competitive serving, but they are more sensitive to:
- Kernel auto-selection mistakes (shape-specific fallbacks, suboptimal choices).
- Scheduler policies (prefill/decode interleaving, batch caps, backpressure) that change the effective shapes and cache behavior.
- GPU SKU differences (H100/H200 vs A100 vs L40S) and driver/CUDA interactions.

This sprint tightens our measurement loop so we can (a) ship reliable defaults and (b) catch regressions before they reach customers.

---

## Scope
### In-scope
**Models** (top hosted chat/completions families):
- Llama-family, Qwen-family, Mistral-family (exact list owned by Benchmark Harness).
- Workload modes: streaming and non-streaming; prefill-heavy vs decode-heavy; mixed prompt lengths.

**Hardware** (perf-lab coverage):
- A100, H100/H200, L40S (MI300X optional if available and does not jeopardize timeline).
- Primary regions used in perf-lab.

**Runtime components**
- Quantized GEMM/attention kernels (FP8/INT8).
- Kernel auto-selection and logging/attribution.
- KV-cache interaction points in quantized decode.
- Scheduler policies that affect prefill/decode interleaving and batching.

**Benchmarking dimensions**
- Microbenchmarks: kernel latency, achieved FLOPs/SM occupancy proxies, memory throughput indicators.
- End-to-end: TTFT (time to first token), TPOT (time per output token), tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latency, and a cost proxy.

---

## Non-goals (explicitly out of scope)
- Broad product/UX work, pricing/packaging changes, or model catalog changes beyond recording recommended quant defaults.
- Large-scale model-quality research. We will run targeted sanity and drift checks to stay within established correctness guardrails.
- Re-architecting the scheduler or replacing kernel libraries wholesale.
- Optimizing for atypical workloads that are not representative of hosted traffic (unless specifically called out as a follow-up item).

---

## Deliverables (end-of-sprint artifacts)
1) **Benchmark methodology document**
   - Pinned environments, clock/power settings, warmup/repetitions, statistical reporting, and common pitfalls.
   - Links to runbook and harness configs.

2) **Benchmark matrix + results artifacts**
   - Model × GPU × quant mode (FP16 baseline, FP8, INT8) with workload presets.
   - Results uploaded in a consistent artifact format with metadata tags (GPU SKU, driver/CUDA, runtime commit, quant profile, scheduler policy).

3) **Performance dashboards + alerting**
   - Quant performance dashboard panels with standard tags.
   - Alerting thresholds for regressions and a documented oncall/triage path.

4) **Perf-canary gating**
   - Nightly quant-perf canary job on a representative subset of GPUs.
   - Regression thresholds + allowlist process for known noisy tests.

5) **Runtime changes (small, high-confidence set)**
   - Kernel tuning fixes, scheduler guardrails, or default config adjustments.
   - Each change must include: before/after measurements, rollback plan, and a safety knob if applicable.

6) **Sprint report (Confluence)**
   - Baselines, deltas from changes, anomaly explanations, recommended defaults, and a follow-up roadmap.

---

## Success metrics
We will consider the sprint successful if all of the following are true:

### A) Measurement quality and repeatability
- Benchmark runs are reproducible in the perf-lab with pinned container/runtime versions and documented environment requirements.
- For the core benchmark set, run-to-run variance is understood and bounded (documented expected noise ranges, with outlier handling).
- Results artifacts contain sufficient metadata to attribute deltas (kernel IDs/selection, quant mode, shapes, clocks).

### B) Coverage
- End-to-end and microbenchmark coverage for each of: A100, H100, and L40S.
- At least one H200 run included if provisioning lands within the sprint (otherwise captured as a follow-up with a dated plan).
- Streaming chat E2E scenario included in the harness (TTFT/TPOT).

### C) Performance improvement (targets)
Targets are directional and must not trade off correctness. We will report per-model and per-GPU deltas and call out where improvements do not generalize.
- **p95 latency**: measurable improvement in at least one high-volume hosted workload (e.g., streaming chat mixed prompt lengths) with no meaningful regression elsewhere.
- **Cost proxy / throughput**: measurable improvement in tokens/sec or effective throughput for quantized paths (prefill and/or decode), with clear attribution.

### D) Correctness/quality guardrails
- INT8/FP8 numerical drift checks in CI (or in the perf-canary pipeline) with documented thresholds and fallback criteria.
- No known high-severity correctness issues remain without a mitigation (disable list, fallback, or safe default).

---

## Primary metrics (at-a-glance)
We will use the definitions from the metrics ADR. This charter calls out the sprint’s headline metrics:
- **TTFT** (Time to First Token): user-perceived responsiveness for streaming.
- **TPOT** (Time per Output Token): decode efficiency and steady-state latency.
- **Tokens/sec**: throughput for a given workload and concurrency.
- **p50/p95/p99 latency**: tail behavior and scheduler effects.
- **Cost proxy**: normalized cost-per-token estimate derived from throughput + GPU SKU assumptions.

---

## Work breakdown and timeline
### Week 1: Spec, environments, baselines
- Finalize benchmark spec: model/workload presets, concurrency, decode parameters.
- Pin perf-lab environment (driver/CUDA, container digest, runtime build flags).
- Land harness updates needed for streaming E2E (TTFT/TPOT) and artifact format.
- Collect baselines for FP16 vs FP8 vs INT8 on initial GPU subset.

### Week 2: Full matrix, fixes, automation, report
- Run full benchmark matrix; investigate anomalies and variance.
- Implement targeted optimizations/config changes (kernel tuning, auto-selection fixes, scheduler policy changes).
- Integrate into perf-canary with thresholds and triage runbook.
- Publish sprint report and recommended defaults; propose follow-up items/ADRs.

---

## Decision-making and change control
- Changes intended to ship in the next runtime release must have: benchmark evidence, correctness guardrail results, and a rollback knob or safe default.
- For any change that affects scheduling policies, we require explicit reporting of tail impact (p95/p99) under mixed prompt lengths.
- Kernel auto-selection changes must include a unit test or shape-coverage test to prevent regressions.

---

## Risks and mitigations
1) **Perf-lab noise / node contention**
   - Mitigation: pinned clocks where supported, dedicated nodes for key runs, documented warmup + repetitions, outlier filtering rules.

2) **H200 provisioning delays**
   - Mitigation: treat H200 as best-effort for this sprint; ensure methodology generalizes; produce a dated follow-up plan if not fully covered.

3) **Correctness regressions in quantized paths**
   - Mitigation: drift checks + fallback criteria; GPU-conditional disables where necessary; do not promote defaults without sign-off.

4) **Overfitting to one workload shape**
   - Mitigation: include both prefill-heavy and decode-heavy workloads; require improvements not to regress the broader matrix beyond thresholds.

5) **Attribution gaps (unclear why we improved/regressed)**
   - Mitigation: kernel-selection and per-phase timing logs; scheduler queue time histograms; consistent metadata tags.

---

## Communication plan
- Daily async update in #eng-runtime (owners post: what changed, what was measured, blockers).
- Mid-sprint readout: end of Week 1 (baseline summary + top risks).
- Final readout: end of Week 2 (results + shipped changes + next steps).

---

## Open questions (to be resolved in Week 1)
- Final list of “top hosted” models and workload presets to freeze for the report.
- Exact perf-canary subset: which GPUs and which scenarios are stable enough for nightly gating.
- Drift thresholds: confirm acceptable numeric drift per model family and per prompt category for INT8/FP8.

---

## Expected artifacts checklist (for sign-off)
- [ ] Methodology doc published and linked from this page
- [ ] Runbook updated for perf-lab execution and troubleshooting
- [ ] Workload presets committed (model/workload matrix)
- [ ] GPU/environment pins documented (driver/CUDA/container digests)
- [ ] Results artifacts uploaded with complete metadata
- [ ] Dashboard panels live + alert routing verified
- [ ] Perf-canary job running nightly with thresholds
- [ ] Final sprint report published with recommendations and follow-ups
